paragraphs.zh: 按：妇人不爱淫者亦爱财，但深畏人知，故不敢为。唯点壮其心，谓人不能知，彼便敢妄为耳。既许从你，彼之遮盖，自然更谨密矣。此羽崇骗姦机巧之一节也。然世情鬼魅，有许多深奸隐慝，何能尽述为戒？特择其近闻者如此。
paragraphs.en: Note: Women who do not love lust still love money, but they deeply fear being found out, so they dare not act. Only when you give them the nerve by saying no one can know will they dare to go ahead. Once they have agreed to you, their cover-up becomes even more careful. This is one of Yu Chong's tricks to seduce a woman. But worldly wickedness has many deep, hidden schemes—how can they all be told as warnings? I only pick what I have recently heard.

stories.title_en: Using Silver to Turn the Tables and Seduce a Woman Drying Paper

paragraphs.zh: 寿山寺，田粮五百石，分为十二房。僧皆富足，都锦衣肉食，饮酒宿娼，更甚俗家。每管寺十餘年，银多欲归，先约家中定姻，在外蓄发为头陀，鬓发可缚网巾，即回娶妻当家矣。每兄去弟来，父亡子继，据为己业，并无异色人得参入。或有畏受家累，不思归俗者，辄择村中愚善佃客有无妻者，出银与代娶。僧先宿一个月，后付与佃客，供不时往宿，僧来则僧之妻，僧去则佃之妇。故谚云：“非僧奸佃妇，乃佃奸僧老婆。”即此俗也。或生子，有全月可认者，则属某；或交错无可辨者，则僧与佃分，各得其一，待十餘岁，即领为侍者，实则亲子也。故僧家云：“灭灯传道，寄姓传宗。”即此也。
paragraphs.en: Shoushan Temple held a grain tax quota of five hundred shi, divided among twelve monastic branches. The monks were all well-off, wearing silk, eating meat, drinking wine, and visiting prostitutes—worse than laypeople. After managing the temple for ten-odd years, if they had accumulated enough silver and wished to return to lay life, they would first arrange a marriage within their family, then let their hair grow out under the guise of wandering ascetics (toutuo). Once their sideburns were long enough to be bound in a hairnet, they returned home, married, and took charge of a household. Brothers succeeded brothers; sons succeeded fathers. They treated the position as hereditary property, and no outsider could intrude. Some who feared the burden of family life and did not wish to return to the lay world would instead select a simple, honest tenant in the village who had no wife, pay silver to marry one for him, and then sleep with her for a month before handing her over to the tenant. She remained at the monk's disposal whenever he visited: when the monk arrived, she was his wife; when he left, she was the tenant's. Hence the saying: "It is not the monk who seduces the tenant's wife—it is the tenant who sleeps with the monk's woman." That was the custom. If a child was born and the timing made paternity clear, the child belonged to that father; if the timing was mixed and uncertain, the monk and the tenant split the children, each taking one. When the boys reached ten or so, the monks brought them into the temple as novice attendants—in truth, their own sons. Hence the monks had a saying: "Put out the lamp to pass on the Dharma; borrow a surname to carry on the line." That is what they meant.

paragraphs.zh: 有一僧，往乡取苗租，其佃户柔懦。见其妇美貌，每挑之便骂，不睬。后冬十月，故买匹好绢，问此妇借剪刀，剪下二尺，曰：“将送人作鞋面。”餘者寄此妇手。两日后复来取绢，借剪刀又剪二尺，将往送人，餘者仍寄之。妇曰：“送甚人，何不全拿去？”僧曰：“只消许多，可长享用。”妇曰：“我代收藏，亦当剪二尺与我。”僧曰：“你若要，便全匹与你，这两尺亦与你，不消送那人矣。”妇曰：“果真乎？”僧曰：“惟恐你不受，我久有意送矣。”两下遂成云雨佳会。僧曰：“你往日骂我，今日何有这好意？”妇曰：“我冬间要做一身衣服，送母亲寿，故不得已从你。后日决不肯矣。”僧曰：“那二尺更要一次。”妇曰：“二尺任你送别人。”僧曰：“取多辞少，你好歹。”
paragraphs.en: One monk went to the village to collect the field rent. The tenant was timid. Seeing that the wife was pretty, the monk made advances whenever he could; she always cursed him and paid him no mind. Later, in the tenth month of winter, he deliberately bought a bolt of good silk, asked this woman to lend scissors, cut off two chi, and said, "I'll give this to someone for shoe tops." He left the rest in her hands. Two days later he came again for the silk, borrowed the scissors, cut another two chi to give someone, and left the rest with her again. The woman said, "Who are you giving it to? Why not take it all?" The monk said, "This much is enough; it will last a long time." The woman said, "If I'm storing it for you, you should cut two chi for me too." The monk said, "If you want it, I'll give you the whole bolt, and these two chi as well—no need to give that other person." The woman said, "Truly?" The monk said, "I only feared you wouldn't take it; I've long meant to give it to you." Then they soon consummated their affair. The monk said, "You used to curse me; why so kind today?" The woman said, "This winter I need a set of clothes as a birthday gift for my mother, so I had no choice but to go along. After this I certainly will not." The monk said, "Those two chi will cost one more time." The woman said, "Give the two chi to someone else." The monk said, "You take much but give back little—what a cunning woman you are!"

paragraphs.zh: 及事完了出房，僧曰：“我要禾稿绞一索用。”妇取付之。僧将稿慢慢绞索。妇催快去，僧曰：“在外何妨？”少顷，佃客回，问曰：“你作索何用？”僧曰：“我有绢大半匹要卖，令正说要造衣，送令岳母寿，以你养的猪，作一两二钱还我绢，将此索牵去。”佃客骂妻曰：“我猪要养，何换此无用绢？急取还他去！”妇取起二尺，将大匹丢出还之，曰：“舍与你！”僧曰：“我还你是价，也不亏你，有甚舍与我？”僧见其取起二尺，知她终是爱财，次月复买蓝绢半匹，并前绢送与之。妇骂曰：“秃骡该入螺蛳地狱，我岂睬你！”僧曰：“正为你常骂我，故意取回，弄你受气。不然，我岂悭吝的？你说要一身衣服送寿，前日止一件衣，今敬剪一件下，成就你事，何故又骂？”妇拒不允，僧再三哀求，只前已有情了，终拒不得，复为受之。后遂通往来，难禁断矣。
paragraphs.en: When they had finished and left the room, the monk said, "I need rice straw to twist a rope." The woman fetched some. The monk twisted the straw slowly. She urged him to hurry up. The monk said, "What harm in being outside?" Soon the tenant returned and asked, "What do you need the rope for?" The monk replied, "I have most of a bolt of silk to sell. Your wife said she wants it to make clothes for your mother-in-law’s birthday, and offered to pay with a pig you raised—two taels and two qian for the silk. This rope is to lead the pig away." The tenant cursed his wife: "I need to raise that pig! Why trade it for useless silk? Give it back at once!" The wife picked up two chi of the silk, threw the rest back, and said, "Take it as a gift!" The monk retorted, "I was paying you a fair price; I wasn’t cheating you. What do you mean, ‘gift’?" Seeing she had kept the two chi, he knew she still loved money. The next month he bought half a bolt of blue silk and brought it along with the earlier piece. The wife cursed, "You shaven beast belong in snail hell—I won’t even look at you!" The monk said, "Precisely because you always curse me, I deliberately took it back to make you angry. Otherwise, would I be stingy? You said you needed a full set of clothes for the birthday. Last time I gave only one piece; now I’ve respectfully cut another so you can finish the job. Why curse again?" She refused. He pleaded again and again. Since they were already intimate, she could not hold out forever and accepted again. After that, they continued their affair; it could no longer be stopped.

paragraphs.zh: 按：此妇性本烈，只为爱其绢，遂至玷身。所谓“枨也欲，焉得刚”是也。人家唯禁止僧道来往，便是好事。若入寺，若拜佛，若子寄僧道姓，此皆耻事，切宜戒之。勿图无影福田，而蹈无穷污垢也。
paragraphs.en: Note: This woman was fiery by nature; only because she loved the silk did she stain herself. As the saying goes, "When desire takes hold, how can one be firm?" Households should simply forbid monks and Daoists from coming and going—that is already a good thing. Entering temples, worshipping Buddha, giving a child a monk's or Daoist's surname—these are all shameful; be sure to avoid them. Do not chase phantom merit, only to step into endless filth.

stories.title_en: A Monk Cuts Silk to Swindle a Tenant's Wife

paragraphs.zh: 有鲁地理，看山颇精。要图一好地，自葬父。寻至宁城，得一佳风水，落在杨乡官坟祠后，既难明买，又难盗葬。闻杨乡官已故，两公子亦欲求地葬父。鲁地理即以此地献，引二公子来看，果好穴情山。不费买，坐向又大利，即用葬父，将银三十两谢地理。鲁客不能谋其地，因欲脱其种。乃租杨公子花园门下住家，用银娶一美妇为妻，与居两个月，对妻曰：“我要出外行地理，难计归程。家下若欠缺薪米，已托主人公子看顾你。此是我恩人，因得他银，故能娶你。我已远出，这两公子若调戏你，随你从他。若与他有情，后日扶持你必厚。但他家多奴仆，切不可与他通。若轻自身，公子必看贱你，后自取困穷，谁来周济你？”又去托两公子：“见得要远出行，地理家下些少，望相周济，归时一一奉还。”
paragraphs.en: There was a geomancer named Lu, quite skilled at reading mountains, who wanted to find a fine gravesite to bury his own father. Searching as far as Ningcheng, he found an auspicious fengshui spot behind the ancestral shrine of the retired official Yang, where it was neither easy to buy openly nor possible to bury in secret. Hearing that Official Yang had passed away and his two sons were also looking for a site to bury their father, Geomancer Lu offered them this spot and led the two young masters to inspect it. It was indeed a fine burial site—it cost them nothing to buy, and its orientation promised great fortune. They buried their father there and rewarded the geomancer with thirty taels of silver. Since Lu could not get the gravesite for himself, he resolved to steal their lineage instead. He rented a house by the garden gate of the Yang sons, used the silver to marry a beautiful woman, and lived with her for two months. Then he told his wife: "I must travel afar to practice geomancy, and I cannot say when I will return. If the household runs short of firewood and rice, I have asked the young masters to look after you. They are my benefactors; it was only because of their silver that I could marry you. While I am away, if these two young masters make advances, you may go along with them. If you win their affection, they will support you generously later on. However, their household has many servants—never have anything to do with the servants. If you cheapen yourself, the young masters will despise you, and you will end up in poverty with no one to help." He also went to ask the two young masters: "I have to travel far away, and my household is left with meager means. Please help look after my wife, and when I return I will repay everything in full."

paragraphs.zh: 公子常往花园，见其妇美，已是动心。地理才去两日，大公子即来其家，调戏其妻。这妇人已承夫嘱，慨然与通，情意好甚。后月餘，次公子亦来戏之，亦从。半年后，鲁地理归，见家中米菜充足，问妻曰：“公子来否？”妻曰：“两人都来，我都纳之。”鲁地理曰：“与这好人交，亦不羞辱你。有吃有穿，有人陪你睡，早晚有人看顾，我虽出外亦安。”妻笑曰：“食用还强你在家时，只你不要吃醋。”地理曰：“是他银娶的，又代我供你，何须妒？但两人迭来，恐你惹毒疮。须与他定一月一个，可无生疮。”
paragraphs.en: The young masters often visited the garden, saw that the wife was beautiful, and were already stirred. Two days after the geomancer left, the elder son came to the house and seduced her. The woman, having received her husband's instructions, readily consented, and they became deeply involved. After about a month, the younger son also came and seduced her; she consented again. Half a year later, Geomancer Lu returned, saw that rice and vegetables were plentiful, and asked his wife: "Did the young masters come?" She replied: "Both came; I took them both." Lu said: "Being with such good men brings you no shame. You have food and clothes, someone to sleep with, people looking after you morning and evening; I can rest easy even when away." The wife laughed: "The provisions are even better than when you were home—just don't get jealous." The geomancer said: "It was their silver that bought you, and they supply your needs in my place—why be jealous? But if both come in turn, you might catch the pox. Set it as one month each, and you won't get sick."

paragraphs.zh: 再次又出外，公子又来。妇人曰：“你两位不时来，恐我成毒疮。须定单月大公子，双月小公子方好。”公子曰：“你说极是。自今某月属某，菜米一应他供给。”不觉经四年，已生两男子，皆两公子血脉矣。鲁地理将命与人推，皆云后当大富贵。因携妻与子辞两公子而归，二人各赠有厚程。后二子长成，皆登科第，实杨姓之风水，被其暗漏去而不知也。
paragraphs.en: When Lu went away again, the young masters came calling once more. The woman said, "If the two of you come at irregular times, I fear I may develop a bad illness. It would be better to set odd months for the elder young master and even months for the younger." The young masters agreed: "You are quite right. From now on, each month belongs to the appointed one, and he shall supply all the vegetables, rice, and provisions." Before they knew it, four years had passed, and she had borne two sons, both of the two young masters' bloodline. Geomancer Lu had their fortunes read, and every diviner predicted great wealth and rank for them in the future. He then took his wife and sons and bade farewell to the two young masters, each of whom gave him generous parting gifts. Later, the two boys grew up and both passed the imperial examinations—in truth, the Yang family's auspicious fengshui had been secretly siphoned away without their ever knowing it.

paragraphs.zh: 按：富贵家子弟，多有好淫人妻小者。或致生子，其风水不无分去。观此地理之脱种，后人可鉴矣。
paragraphs.en: Note: Sons of rich families often lust after other men's wives. If children result, their fengshui is inevitably split away. Observe how the lineage was cheated out of its seed—later generations should take warning from this.

paragraphs.zh: 有一富家子，往佃户家取租，见其妇美，累挑之。妇不敢从，密报于婆。婆曰：“他富家子，若与他有子，后日亦讨得吃。”富子后又挑之，妇即允，与入房中解衣。富子曰：“往时累说不从，今何故便肯？”妇曰：“已对婆婆说过了。”富子曰：“你婆要拿奸么？”妇曰：“非也！婆曰傍你富家种，若有儿，亦讨得吃。”富子一闻漏种话，猛然自省曰：“不可！不可！”连说四句“不可”，因转言曰：“我非真欲奸，只爱你生得好，故与耍耳。今送银三钱，与你买粉，我不污你也。”淫情已动，驰归家，夜与妻交。其夜受胎，后生一男，长中进士，官受知县。
paragraphs.en: A rich young man went to a tenant's house to collect rent, saw the wife was beautiful, and propositioned her repeatedly. She dared not consent and secretly told her mother-in-law. The mother-in-law said, "He's a rich man's son; if you bear him a child, later we'll have something to eat." The rich man propositioned her again; she agreed, and they went into the room to undress. He asked, "You always refused before; why agree now?" She replied, "I've already told my mother-in-law." He asked, "Does she want to catch us in the act?" She said, "No. She said to lean on your rich-family seed; if there's a son, we'll have something to eat." Upon hearing this talk of sowing seed, he suddenly realized his folly, shouting, "No! No!" four times. Then he changed his tone: 'I didn't really mean to harm you; I only admired your beauty, so I was just playing. Here are three qian of silver for powder; I won't defile you.' Still stirred by lust, he hurried home and slept with his wife that night. She conceived immediately; later, a son was born who grew up to pass the jinshi examination and became a county magistrate.

paragraphs.zh: 初上任日，天晴日朗，忽见官堂四大柱上，各有两个“不可”金字，心中忧曰：“此必不可任此官也。”谨慎做一季官，便推病辞官养亲，匆然归。父惊问故，答曰：“因上任日，见四个‘不可’金字，恐非吉光，故辞官归养。”父曰：“养亲官在亦可。”经一夜，父思到大喜，呼其子曰：“你见四‘不可’金字，此大吉兆，你官必高也。我少年时，挑一佃妇，已允矣。临行事时，他说要傍我好种，我猛省起，连说四句‘不可’，遂不肯苟合。其夜归后即生汝，此天报我不淫人妇之德。若是凶兆，何故是金字？又何故四个‘不可’，与我昔言相应也？此是好兆矣。”儿曰：“是也。”随即写书托同年，次年复起官。后官至侍郎，一门贵盛。
paragraphs.en: On the first day of taking office, under a clear sky, he suddenly saw two golden characters "Must Not" on each of the four great pillars of the hall. He worried: "I must not take this post." He served carefully for one season, then feigned illness and resigned to care for his parents, hurrying home. His father asked in alarm. He answered: "On the day I took office, I saw four golden "Must Not" signs; fearing they were not auspicious, I resigned to return home and care for you." The father said: "You can care for your parents while still in office." After a night, the father thought it over and was overjoyed. He called his son: 'Those four golden "Must Not" are a great auspicious sign; your career will soar. When I was young, I courted a tenant's wife; she had already agreed. At the moment of consummation, she said she wanted to rely on me as a proper husband. I suddenly came to my senses and said "Must Not" four times, refusing to go through with it. That very night after I returned, you were conceived. This is Heaven rewarding me for not defiling another man's wife. If it were an ill omen, why golden characters? Why four "Must Not," matching what I once said? This is a good sign.' The son agreed. He immediately wrote to a fellow examinee; the next year he was reinstated. Later he rose to Vice Minister, and the whole family flourished.

paragraphs.zh: 看此节，可见富贵家子弟不可漏种于人矣。有乡官知县，生四男，皆为秀才，聪明俊伟。一日，乡官卒。地理为择一葬地，风水甚佳，曰：“六年两科内，四位公子当尽登科第。”六年后，地理来取谢。三长公子都中去为官，独四公子在家款待地理，敬问曰：“承先生许我四人皆发科，今三位兄果中矣。论才学，我更高于兄，独不中，何故？”明日，地理同四公子再登坟细看，曰：“论此地，虽几兄弟皆当中，其间不中者，必有故。”公子恳问何故，地理曰：“令先尊几岁生你？”公子曰：“先父生我时年六十，后七十四岁卒，今又六年矣。”又问曰：“令堂当时几岁？”公子曰：“其时三十岁。”地理摇头曰：“我知之矣。”公子曰：“先生知何缘故？”地理曰：“休怪我说。公子必欲中，须问太夫人，你是何人血脉？”公子会其意，夜设盛席，慢慢劝母醉饮。至二更后，吩咐亲人并奴婢等各先睡。四下无人，公子跪曰：“儿有所禀，不敢言。不知母亲愿我中否？”母曰：“三哥子都中了，我愿你中极切。有甚好歹事，但说无妨。”公子曰：“地理说我不是爹爹亲血脉，故不中。必须知谁实生我，方可中。”母本爱幼子，静夜又无人，酒后又醉了，不觉吐言曰：“地理果高见。彼时你父已六十，衙中某门子后生标致，我实与他生你。”公子已得实，次日谋于地理。地理曰：“须到彼处谋门子骸骨来，附葬旁，来科即中矣。”公子依言，往取而葬之，次科果中。
paragraphs.en: This passage illustrates that sons of wealthy families must be careful not to sow their seed with another man. A retired official who had served as magistrate had four sons, all licentiates (xiucai), clever and handsome. One day the official died. A geomancer selected a burial site with excellent fengshui, saying: "Within six years and two examination cycles, all four young masters will pass." Six years later, the geomancer came to collect his reward. The three elder sons had all passed and become officials; only the fourth son remained at home entertaining the geomancer. He respectfully asked: "You promised all four of us would pass. My three brothers have indeed succeeded. In talent I am even superior to them; why do I alone fail?" The next day, the geomancer and the fourth son climbed the grave to examine it closely. The geomancer said: "By this site, all the brothers should pass; if one has not, there must be a reason." The son pressed him for an explanation. The geomancer asked: "How old was your late father when he begot you?" The son replied: "Father was sixty when I was born; he died at seventy-four; that makes another six years now." He asked again: "How old was your mother then?" The son said: "Thirty." The geomancer shook his head: "I know now." The son asked: "What do you know?" The geomancer said: "Do not take offense. If you wish to pass, you must ask the old lady whose blood you truly are." The son understood. That night he set up a lavish feast and slowly got his mother drunk. After the second watch, he instructed relatives and servants to retire first. With no one around, he knelt and said: "I have something I dare not speak. Does Mother wish me to pass?" The mother said: "Your three brothers all passed; I desire your success most of all. Whatever it is, good or bad, just say it." The son said: "The geomancer says I am not Father's own flesh and blood, which is why I don't pass. I must know who truly fathered me before I can succeed." The mother loved her youngest son; it was a quiet night, no one else was present, and she was drunk—she let slip: "The geomancer sees truly. At that time your father was already sixty. A certain page in the yamen was young and handsome; I actually bore you by him." The son obtained the truth. The next day he consulted the geomancer. The geomancer said: "You must go there, retrieve the page's bones, and bury them beside the grave; in the next cycle you will pass." The son followed these instructions, fetched and buried them; in the next cycle he indeed passed.

paragraphs.zh: 看此节，可见暗中杂种，人不及知，故有共风水而贵贱悬隔者，其中不无难言处也。
paragraphs.en: This passage reveals how illegitimate offspring can be concealed, unknown to others—hence why some share the same ancestral fortune yet end up worlds apart in rank. There is always something unspeakable about such matters.

paragraphs.zh: 又解某之父，血衰无子。其母夏月热甚，着单裙睡于床。家蓄有猴公，往奸之。惊醒欲推去，猴欲啮欲抓，推去不得。睡熟神旺，不觉淫情动，即有孕。解父归，妻与言被猴奸之故，曰：“此异物，须杀之。”猴既奸后心亏，走于后门大桃树上，不肯下。解父故与妻戏于树下。猴见人色喜，方下树来。解父槌杀之，即埋于桃树下。后解某生，极聪明伶俐，但跳跃倒地，若猴状。解母心知为猴种也。以无别子，故不杀之。八岁父死，地理为择葬曰：“此地极佳，当出神童才子。此子虽不才，但三年后可登高第。”过三年后，地理复来。解母曰：“汝说三年后此子知变，今轻狂如前，奈何？”地理再往坟细看，归问曰：“此子是安人亲生的，抑妾生乎？”解母曰：“此子非亲生，是邻家丫头与猴生的，欲弃之，我以无子，故血抱以养。”地理曰：“欲此子成器，须得猴骨在，附葬此冢之旁，后日还昌你家。”解母往树下掘之，其骨犹在。特与地理曰：“邻人尚留骨在，当如何处？”地理教择吉日葬之。再三年，果举神童，后为一代名人。（此闻其乡陈地理所传。）
paragraphs.en: Another case: the father of a certain Xie had failing vitality and no son. In the summer heat, his mother was sleeping on the bed in a thin unlined skirt when a male monkey kept by the household came and violated her. Startled awake, she tried to push it off, but the monkey bared its teeth and claws to bite and scratch, so she could not push it away. As she drifted back into a deep sleep, her spirits stirred, passion rose in her despite herself, and she conceived. When Xie's father returned home, his wife told him how the monkey had violated her and said, "This unnatural creature must be killed." Feeling guilty after the deed, the monkey had climbed up a tall peach tree outside the back gate and refused to come down. Xie's father deliberately sported with his wife beneath the tree; seeing them make love, the monkey grew excited and climbed down, whereupon Xie's father clubbed it to death and buried it under the peach tree. Later, when young Xie was born, he was extraordinarily bright and quick-witted, yet he hopped and tumbled on the ground just like a monkey. His mother knew in her heart that he was the monkey's seed, but having no other son, she could not bear to kill him. When the boy was eight, his father died. A geomancer chose a burial site and said, "This site is superb; it will produce a child prodigy and a man of great talent. Though the boy seems unruly now, in three years he will rise to high rank." Three years later, the geomancer returned. Mother Xie said, "You said that after three years this boy would mend his ways, yet he is still as wild and flighty as before—what can be done?" The geomancer went back to inspect the grave carefully, then returned and asked, "Madam, was this boy born of your own womb, or of a concubine?" Mother Xie replied, "He is not my own; a neighbor's maid bore him by a monkey and wanted to abandon him. Because I had no son, I took him in from birth and raised him as my own." The geomancer said, "If you want this boy to amount to something, the monkey's bones must be buried beside this grave; then in days to come he will bring great prosperity to your house." Mother Xie dug beneath the peach tree and found the bones still there. She went expressly to tell the geomancer, "The neighbors still have the bones; how should we handle it?" The geomancer instructed her to choose an auspicious day to bury them. After another three years, the boy was indeed recommended as a child prodigy and later became a celebrated figure of his age. (Heard from Geomancer Chen of that district.)

paragraphs.zh: 看此节，可见风水之效，捷如影响。人家得好地者，子孙宜守礼法，不可淫欲败德，致漏脉于人也。
paragraphs.en: This passage shows that the effect of feng shui is as immediate as a shadow and an echo. Families who secure a good site must ensure their descendants observe rites and laws; they must not ruin their virtue through lust, lest they squander the family fortune for others.

stories.title_en: A Geomancer Leaves His Wife Behind to Steal a Fine Lineage

paragraphs.zh: 宁城一人，姓李名英，年二十餘岁，聪明脱洒，惟耽酒色。常买夏布，往苏州阊门外，寓牙人陈四店。其店兼卖白酒。邻家林廷节，常遣婢京季来买酒。季年方十八，国色娇媚。李英爱之，因而调戏成奸，买簪圈等送之。同店多有谏其勿惹祸者。英与季两少相爱，情深意美，哪肯割断？后廷节察知季与英有奸，呼季责曰：“你与李客私通，我姑恕汝。可密窥英银藏于何处，偷来置些衣装与你，后得享用。”
paragraphs.en: In Ningcheng lived a man named Li Ying, over twenty years old, clever and slick, yet addicted to wine and women. He often bought summer cloth, went outside Chang Gate in Suzhou, and lodged at broker Chen Si's shop, which also sold white liquor. A neighbor, Lin Tingjie, frequently sent his maid Jing Ji to buy wine. Ji was only eighteen, a rare beauty. Li Ying fell for her, teased her into an affair, and bought hairpins and bangles for her. Others in the shop often warned him not to court disaster. Ying and Ji were both young and deeply in love—who would sever such a bond? Later, Tingjie discovered their affair. He called Ji and scolded her: "You have been secretly with Guest Li; I will let you off this once. Secretly watch where Ying hides his silver, steal some, and I will get you clothes to enjoy later."

paragraphs.zh: 一日，英饮酒娼家。季潜开英房，盗去银一百餘两。及英回店，知银有失，向店主逼取。客伙吴伦曰：“你房内有银，不可远饮娼家；即饮亦宜早归。今荡饮致失，何干主人事？今午见京季入你房中，必此女偷去。你可告于官，我与店主为证。”
paragraphs.en: One day, while Ying was out drinking at a brothel, the courtesan Jing Ji quietly unlocked his room and stole over a hundred taels of silver. When Ying returned to the inn and discovered the silver missing, he pressed the innkeeper to make good the loss. Fellow lodger Wu Lun said, "When you keep silver in your room, you shouldn't go drinking far off at a brothel; even if you do, you should return early. You went out carousing and lost it—what does that have to do with the innkeeper? At noon today I saw Jing Ji go into your room; it must be that woman who stole it. You can report this to the officials, and the innkeeper and I will testify for you."

paragraphs.zh: 英待两日，季不来店，乃告于府。廷节诉英欺奸伊婢，情露惧告，先以失银诬抵。本府张爷审问于证，吴伦、陈四证曰：“亲见季入英房，盗去银是实。”张爷诘曰：“客人房、室女床，二者岂容妄入？季入英房，汝等见何不阻？”伦曰：“英与季私通，亦是实，故英未在店，开门而盗。”张爷审出此情，知银系季偷是的；奈廷节乃府庠生，季考取之第二，只依廷节所诉，断曰：“既有奸情，则失银系是抵饰。以英不合欺奸侍婢，虚词抵赖。陈四为牙，知有奸情，何不谏英早改？待事败而犹偏证，各拟杖惩。”
paragraphs.en: Ying waited two days; Ji did not come to the shop, so he reported it to the prefecture. Tingjie claimed Ying had seduced his maid. When the affair was exposed, fearing prosecution, Ji had first falsely accused Ying of losing silver to cover his tracks. Prefect Zhang questioned the witnesses. Wu Lun and Chen Si testified: "We saw Ji enter Ying's room with our own eyes; it is true he stole the silver." Prefect Zhang pressed: "A guest's room and a maiden's bed—neither should be entered lightly. If you saw Ji enter Ying's room, why didn't you stop him?" Lun said: "Ying and Ji having an affair is also true; so when Ying wasn't in the shop, Ji opened the door and stole." Prefect Zhang found this out and knew the silver was indeed stolen by Ji; but Tingjie was a student of the prefectural school, ranked second in the last exam, so he followed Tingjie's complaint and ruled: "Since there was an illicit affair, the lost silver is merely a covering excuse. Li Ying was wrong to seduce a serving maid and then lie. Chen Si, as broker, knew of the affair; why didn't he advise Ying to stop sooner? After it blew up, he still testified one-sidedly. Each is sentenced to beating."

paragraphs.zh: 按：此审李英甚枉。特为客旅，宜谨慎自持，岂有奸人侍婢而不取祸者！今店中多有以妻女引诱客人，成奸后赖其财本者。切宜识透此套，勿入其骗可也。
paragraphs.en: Note: This judgment was very unjust to Li Ying. Especially as a traveling merchant, one should be careful and self-restrained; who has an affair with someone's maid and does not bring disaster? Nowadays many shops use wives and daughters to lure guests; after the affair they cheat them of their capital. See through this trick; do not fall into it.

stories.title_en: A Wicked Maid Steals the Silver

paragraphs.zh: 经纪廖三号龙潭者，有女名淑姬，年方二八，尚未配人。容如月姊，貌赛花仙，真个女子中班头，绝世无双者。客人张鲁，年二十餘岁，磊落俊雅，颇谙诗书，浪迹江湖。一日，买闽笋数十担，在廖三店中发卖。不时遇风，都放帐未收。日久，见其女丰姿娇媚，日夜想慕，不能安枕。奈廖三家中人众，难以动手。而女亦时于门后偷眼觑鲁。鲁以目挑之，女为俯首作娇羞态。二人情意已通，只阳臺路隔，鹊桥难渡矣。
paragraphs.en: Broker Liao San, alias Longtan, had a daughter named Shuji, just sixteen, still unmarried. Her face shone like the moon goddess, her beauty rivaling a flower immortal—truly the leader among women, unmatched in the world. The merchant Zhang Lu, a little over twenty, handsome and elegant, well-versed in poetry and books, drifted from place to place. One day he bought several dozen loads of Fujian bamboo shoots and sold them at Liao San's shop. Due to frequent delays, the goods were sold on credit, with the silver still unpaid. Over time, seeing the daughter's charming looks, he longed day and night and could not sleep. But Liao San's household was crowded, making it hard to act. The girl also sometimes peeked at Lu from behind the door. Lu made eyes at her; she lowered her head in a shy pose. Their hearts were already joined, but the path remained blocked, like the Magpie Bridge hard to cross.

paragraphs.zh: 一日，廖三家中早起炊饭，与商人上乡讨帐。张鲁心喜，乘机潜入其房，与廖女成姦。偷情之后，时有私会。
paragraphs.en: One day, Liao San's household rose early to prepare breakfast. He then went with some merchants to the countryside to collect debts. Zhang Lu, delighted by this opportunity, slipped into her room and committed adultery with Liao's daughter. Afterward, they continued to meet privately from time to time.

paragraphs.zh: 其母知之，与夫商议曰：“吾女几多豪门求婚，未肯轻许。今被鼠客所玷，须密捕杀之，以消其恨。”廖三曰：“不可。凡妻与人私通，当场捉获，併斩呈官，律方无罪。今女与人通姦，併杀则不忍；单杀客人，被罪不至死，岂死无后话？现今笋帐已完，其银皆在我手。密窥女与姦时，当场捉之，打他半死，以锁繫住，勒其供状，怕他不把笋银献我，彼时亦何说？”妻然之。
paragraphs.en: When the mother found out, she conferred with her husband: "How many wealthy families have sought our daughter's hand, and we refused to give her lightly! Now she has been defiled by this rat of a traveling merchant. We must secretly catch and kill him to vent our anger." Liao San said, "No. Only when a wife commits adultery and you catch them in the act and kill both on the spot does the law hold you blameless. Here it is our daughter having an illicit affair: I cannot bear to kill them both, and if we kill only the merchant, his offense does not carry the death penalty—how could we kill him without facing serious consequences afterward? Right now the bamboo-shoot accounts are settled, and all his silver is in my hands. Let us secretly watch for when our daughter meets him again, catch them in the act, beat him half to death, chain him up, and force a written confession out of him. Won't he have to forfeit his bamboo-shoot silver to us then? And what would he dare say afterward?" His wife agreed.

paragraphs.zh: 未数日，张鲁果堕其术。鲁曰：“此是我不良。银须以一半还我便罢，不然吾不甘心。”廖三不允，鲁遂告于府，批刑馆。吴爷审出实情，问淑姬：“曾许配人否？”对曰：“未配。”又问鲁：“曾娶否？”鲁已有发妻，乃诳曰：“发妻已死，尚未再娶。”吴爷断曰：“汝二人既未成婚，须断合之，以所勒银准作财礼。”廖三曰：“奸人室女而得成婚，后何以儆？”吴爷曰：“汝牙家常以妻女赖人姦而脱其银，吾岂不知？若不配合，须将汝女官卖，将银究论；张鲁合惩通姦之罪耳。”鲁曰：“一女子安值财礼一百餘两？须判一半还我，准与其女为奁。”吴爷曰：“为商而嫖花街柳巷，尚宜有节；主人室女，岂容欺姦？”鲁且感且哭，尽丧其本，止得一女，又无盘缠可带，即转嫁银三十两而归。
paragraphs.en: Within days Zhang Lu fell into the trap. Lu said: "This is my own fault. Give me back half the silver and let it go; otherwise I cannot rest." Liao San refused, so Lu sued at the prefecture, where the case was remanded to the court. Judge Wu uncovered the truth and asked Shuji: "Have you been betrothed?" She replied: "Not yet." He then asked Lu: "Are you married?" Lu already had a wife but lied: "My first wife is dead; I have not remarried." Judge Wu ruled: "Since neither of you is married, you must be joined; the silver extorted shall count as the bride-price." Liao San argued: "If a man who seduces a virgin can then marry her, how will others be warned?" Judge Wu retorted: "You matchmakers often use wives and daughters to trap guests into affairs and cheat them out of their silver—do I not know? If they are not matched, I will have your daughter sold by the government and investigate the silver; Zhang Lu will still be punished for adultery." Lu protested: "How is one girl worth over a hundred taels of bride-price? Order half returned to me, counting as her dowry." Judge Wu declared: "A merchant visiting brothels should still observe limits; how dare he seduce the host's virgin daughter?" Lu felt both gratitude and shame, weeping; he lost all his capital, gained only a wife, and had no travel funds left, so he sold her hand for thirty taels and returned home.

paragraphs.zh: 按：牙家纵容妻女与客人成姦，后脱其财本，此常套也。惜此女不知，为父母作货；张鲁亦不知，而落此套中。犹幸吴爷断与成婚，虽失利，犹得妇也。惜其财本稀少，不得同此女归耳。后之为商者，断合事本难期望，则脱姦宜慎防之。
paragraphs.en: Note: Brokers who connive with their wives and daughters to commit adultery with guests, then cheat them out of their capital—this is a common trick. Pity this girl did not know she was being sold by her parents; Zhang Lu also did not know and fell into the trap. Luckily Judge Wu ordered them married; though he lost his money, he still got a wife. Pity his capital was so thin he could not take the girl home. For merchants in the future: relying on such legal resolutions is fundamentally unrealistic; one must be very careful to guard against being cheated through an affair.

stories.title_en: Seduction of a Broker's Daughter Ends in a Swindle

paragraphs.zh: 两妯娌并坐，适有卖油者过。婶石氏曰：“家下要油用，奈无银可买。”姆左氏曰：“先秤油来，约后还银未迟。”石氏叫入买油，秤定二斤矣。曰：“男人未在家，过两日来接银。”后两日卖油者来，婶曰：“无银，何以处？”姆曰：“再约三日。”婶以此言退之去。又三日，婶曰：“你教我先秤油，今竟无银。你讨些借我还。”姆曰：“你肯依我教，还他何难？”婶曰：“我凡事常依你，把甚物还？”姆曰：“我看卖油后生俊俏，你青年貌美，和他相好一次，油何消还？”婶曰：“恐你后日说。”姆曰：“是我教你，怎敢说？我避在房中，你自去为之。”
paragraphs.en: Two sisters-in-law were sitting together when an oil seller passed by. The younger sister-in-law, Lady Shi, said, "We need oil in the house, but we have no silver to buy it." The elder sister-in-law, Lady Zuo, said, "Have him weigh out the oil first; paying him later will be soon enough." Lady Shi called him in and had two catties of oil weighed out. She said, "Our men aren't home; come back in two days for the silver." Two days later the oil seller returned. The younger sister-in-law said, "There is no silver—what shall we do?" The elder said, "Put him off for another three days." The younger used these words to send him away. After three more days the younger said, "You told me to have the oil weighed out first, and now there is still no silver. Lend me a little so I can pay him." The elder said, "If you are willing to do as I teach you, paying him back will be no trouble at all." The younger said, "I always follow your lead in everything—what should I give him to pay for it?" The elder said, "I see that young oil seller is handsome, and you are young and pretty. Be intimate with him once, and why would you need to pay for the oil?" The younger said, "I am afraid you might talk about it afterward." The elder said, "I am the one who taught you—how would I dare speak of it? I will step into the inner room to stay out of the way while you go and do it."

paragraphs.zh: 少顷，卖油者到。石氏思无计可退，强作笑脸，出迎曰：“两次约你接银，奈何无可措办，不如把我还你罢。”卖油者见其眉开眼笑，亦起淫心曰：“你家内有人，莫非哄我？”石氏曰：“丈夫去耕田，伯姆在邻家绩麻。因无人，故与你耍言。”卖油者放心，与入房去。左氏听已拴房门，即密出，将两半篓油倾起，把两半篓水注入，再到房门密听。婶曰：“完了，起去。”卖油者曰：“与我停停。”左氏手持麻筐，跳身出大门外，故扬言曰：“今日尚未午，何耕田的回了？”卖油者闻人言，忙出挑油，恰相遇于门外。左氏问曰：“婶婶油还你否？”卖油者连应曰：“还了！还了！”即挑过一村卖。左氏知其必再来，站在大门候。
paragraphs.en: Shortly the oil seller arrived. Shi had no way to put him off. She forced a smile, came out to meet him, and said, "Twice I set a date to pay you, but I still can't raise the money. Better I return your silver." The oil seller saw her beaming, and lust rose in him: "There are people in your house—are you tricking me?" Shi said, "My husband’s in the fields; my mother-in-law is next door spinning hemp. There’s no one here, so I was teasing you." The oil seller was reassured and went into the room with her. Zuo heard the door bolted, slipped out, poured the oil from both half-baskets, filled both with water, then went back to listen at the door. The Aunt said, "Done—get up." The oil seller said, "Stay with me a bit." Zuo, hemp basket in hand, jumped out the main gate and deliberately shouted, "It’s not even noon—how is the field-worker back already?" The oil seller heard, hurriedly came out with his carrying-pole, and met her at the gate. Zuo asked, "Did my aunt pay you for the oil?" The oil seller quickly said, "Paid! Paid!" and carried it off to sell in the next village. Zuo knew he would come back, and waited at the main gate.

paragraphs.zh: 近午，卖油者向前。左氏曰：“你尚在此？我婶婶的弟挑桶来打涝，见油一担在宅，家并无人，只婶房有人笑话，疑与卖油人有奸，将油倾在桶去，把半篓水注满，归报其母，母子径来拿奸。及来时，挑油的已去，正在此猜疑。叵知你在此，必拿你作对。”卖油者便行。左氏扯住曰：“我报你知，你须谢我。”卖油者曰：“明日寄两斤油与你。”
paragraphs.en: Near noon, the oil seller returned. Zuo said: "You're still here? My sister-in-law's brother came carrying buckets to fetch water. He saw a load of oil left in the house with no one around, except for some laughter coming from her room. Suspicious, he thought she was having an affair with the oil seller. He poured the oil into his buckets and filled the remaining space with water, then went home to tell his mother. Mother and son rushed over to catch them in the act. By the time they arrived, the oil carrier had already fled; they are still guessing about what happened. If they knew you were here, they would surely make you the target." The oil seller tried to leave. Zuo grabbed him: "I tipped you off; you ought to thank me." The oil seller replied: "Tomorrow I'll send you two jin of oil."

paragraphs.zh: 过数日，果寄油来。姆又变说，持与婶曰：“前日我在门站，卖油者复从门前过。我故耍之曰：‘婶婶说油银未还，你适间慌忙说还了，必有缘故。我在此等报叔叔。’卖油者心虚，许我两斤油，今果寄来。此是你换来的，须当补你。”婶曰：“似此半时光景，也是四斤油用，多谢指教。”姆曰：“你若依我，更有别享用处。”
paragraphs.en: After several days, he indeed sent the oil. The sister-in-law changed her story, took it to her brother's wife, and said, "The other day I was standing at the gate when the oil seller passed by again. I teased him, saying, 'My sister-in-law says the silver for the oil hasn't been paid yet, yet you hurriedly claimed it was settled—there must be a reason. I'm waiting here to tell my brother.' Feeling guilty, he promised me two catties of oil, and now he has sent them. Since you traded your favors for this, I ought to share it with you." Her brother's wife replied, "In that half hour I got four catties of oil to use—thank you for showing me the way." The sister-in-law said, "If you listen to me, there are even better things to enjoy."

paragraphs.zh: 少顷，有人叫卖肉。姆婶二人叫入，各秤二斤，吩咐再来接银。三日，屠子来接。伯姆秤银七分还之，婶的再约两日。至期，屠子来。伯姆曰：“你依前日套子还他，我方便入房内去。”石氏出，笑对屠子曰：“借你肉，无银可还。今日无人在家，不如把我肉还你。”屠子见其美貌，嬉嬉笑曰：“我只要你腰间些些肉。”石氏曰：“全身都允你，何惜些些？”屠子搂抱入房干事。伯姆潜出，把一担肉都搬入讫，默坐在肉箩边。
paragraphs.en: Soon someone called out selling meat. The two women called him in, each weighed out two jin, and told him to return for the silver. Three days later, the butcher came to collect. The elder woman weighed out silver of seven-tenths purity to pay him; the younger's portion was set for two more days. When the time came, the butcher arrived. The elder said, "Pay him with the same trick as before; I'll conveniently slip into the room." Shi came out, smiled at the butcher, and said, "I borrowed your meat and have no silver to pay. Today no one is home; better I pay you with my own flesh." The butcher saw how pretty she was, grinned, and said, "I only want a little bit of the meat around your waist." Shi replied, "The whole body is yours—why begrudge a little?" The butcher pulled her into the room and got down to business. The elder slipped out, moved the entire load of meat inside, and sat silently by the meat hampers.

paragraphs.zh: 屠子与石氏欢罢而出，问曰：“我肉在哪里去？”左氏曰：“叔叔挑与里老去了。”屠子曰：“何得偷我肉？”左氏曰：“你好大胆！叔叔归，见肉担在此，入房门来又闭住，只闻你两人嘻嘻笑话，知是你奸他妻，叫我看住房门。我不好听你动静，故坐在此。你且略坐，停会偷肉的便来了。”屠子挑起空箩便走。左氏扯住曰：“把一肉刀与我做当头。”屠子曰：“托你方便，明日送两斤肉与你。”左氏放手，屠子飞步奔去。
paragraphs.en: The butcher finished his tryst with Shi and came out, asking: "Where has my meat gone?" Zuo replied, "Uncle took it to the village head." The butcher said, "How dare you steal my meat?" Zuo retorted, "You've got nerve! Uncle returned, saw the meat load here, noticed the bedroom door shut, heard you two laughing, realized you were with his wife, and ordered me to guard the door. I didn't want to eavesdrop on your antics, so I sat here. Just sit a moment; the man who stole your meat will be back soon." The butcher lifted the empty baskets and started to run. Zuo grabbed him: "Give me a meat knife as collateral." The butcher said, "Thanks for your help; tomorrow I'll send you two jin of meat." Zuo let go, and the butcher fled at full speed.

paragraphs.zh: 婶埋怨曰：“都是你教我干此事。今丈夫知道，怎么是好？”姆曰：“你不该把师父摊出来。只要你肯食肉，此事何难遮盖？”婶曰：“有甚计策，快说出来。”姆入房，拖一腿肉出，又入拖一腿，曰：“你食肉乎？你报丈夫乎？”婶曰：“你偷肉，不该惊死我。”姆曰：“我惊那人；不惊他去，怎得他肉？”
paragraphs.en: The younger complained: "It was you who taught me to do this. Now my husband knows—what then?" The elder said, "You shouldn't have exposed your master like that. As long as you're willing to eat the meat, covering this up is easy." The younger said, "What's the plan? Quick, tell me." The elder went in, dragged out one leg of meat, then another: "Will you eat the meat, or tell your husband?" The younger said, "You stole the meat! You shouldn't have scared me half to death." The elder replied, "I scared him away; if I hadn't scared him off, how would we have gotten his meat?"

paragraphs.zh: 两妯娌将肉煮来，把酒对吃。婶曰：“真是一日不识羞，三日吃饱饭。”姆曰：“不是如此说，是半时得快活，一月吃酒肉。”二人呵呵，饱吃一顿，餘者烟干后食。
paragraphs.en: The two sisters-in-law boiled the meat and shared a meal with wine. The younger said, "Truly: one day without shame brings three days of full bellies." The elder replied, "Not so—half an hour of pleasure buys a month of wine and meat." They laughed heartily, ate their fill, and ate the rest after it had been smoked.

paragraphs.zh: 后数日，屠子经过，左氏出，支肉二斤，屠子速行。左氏曰：“亏我婶娘前日被一餐粗打，也该送二斤与她。”屠子将一片丢来，曰：“托你转上，我不得暇。”左氏手提两吊肉，入对婶娘说知，又将来作乐。婶曰：“我会养汉，不如你会光棍。”以后奸门一开，不可胜记。
paragraphs.en: A few days later, the butcher passed by. Lady Zuo came out and asked for two catties of meat on credit, and the butcher hurried on. Lady Zuo said, "My poor younger sister-in-law took a rough beating because of you the other day—you ought to give her two catties too." The butcher tossed over a cut of meat and said, "Please pass this along to her for me; I have no time to spare." Carrying the two strips of meat in hand, Lady Zuo went inside, told her younger sister-in-law the whole story, and brought the meat out for another merry feast. The younger sister-in-law said, "I may know how to keep a lover, but you are even better at playing the swindler!" Once the door to illicit affairs was opened, what followed was more than could ever be recorded.

paragraphs.zh: 按：石婶不过呆妇人，左姆乃狡猾巧妇；若是男子，当为大棍。遇此巧妇，愚者何不落其圈套？故不唯男子当择交，妇人尤当与良女相伴也。
paragraphs.en: Note: Aunt Shi was only a dull woman; Elder Zuo was a cunning, clever one. Had she been a man, she would have been a master of the game. Meeting such a clever woman, how would a fool not fall into her trap? So not only should men choose their company; women especially should keep company with good women.

stories.title_en: Luring a Sister-in-Law into Adultery to Cheat Them Out of Oil and Meat

paragraphs.zh: 乡间有一殷实村老，谷豆满仓，鸡鸭成群。只极是村恶，不知礼体。娶一田家女为媳妇，年少貌美，便思爬灰。只怕老妈严厉约束，家法整肃，积年不敢发。
paragraphs.en: In the countryside there was a well-off old villager, granaries full of grain and beans, chickens and ducks in flocks. He was extremely rustic and coarse, with no sense of propriety. He married a farm girl as daughter-in-law, young and pretty, and thought of sleeping with her. He only feared the old lady’s strict control; household rules were tight, and for years he dared not act.

paragraphs.zh: 一日，老妈邻家请饮，村老便调戏其妇。拒不从，遂行强抱。其妇喊起骂出，去外家只十里，便徒步奔告于母。母系村妇，惫赖愤怒，同女来。这村老见媳妇奔告外家，忙叫老妈回，以实情吐告，商量何以抵对。老妈心忖：“亲家村鲁，必不来，惟姻母惫赖必来。”已思有计笼之，故反言要老公曰：“恭喜你，喜事到矣！”村老曰：“往事已错，何须再题。你往日常能干，我凡事皆听你。今须救我，忽致破家。”老妈曰：“何止破家，你该死矣！我今救你来，你越胆大。若听我言，事过再勿起此野意，不但救你，且有好事抬举你。”村老曰：“不愿抬举，只救得这一遭，再不敢起恶意。若再有此，天诛地灭！”老妈曰：“既肯誓过，饶你这遭。你取银四两，作二锭，伏在外客房中，覆大下。若姻母来，我叫她在房来洗澡。你听其洗完，从下出，以两锭银付她两手。她必定拿住，推拒你不得，你便强奸一次。走出外去，事便息矣。”村老曰：“若奸她，则挑她女是真矣。”老妈曰：“你勿管，后事在我身。”村老依言，藏入大去。
paragraphs.en: One day, the old mother-in-law was invited next door for a drink, and the old villager took the chance to make advances to his daughter-in-law. When she refused, he tried to force himself on her. Shouting and cursing, the young wife broke free and ran out. Her parents' home was only ten li away, so she ran there on foot to tell her mother. Her mother was a fierce, shrewish village woman, and she marched straight over with her daughter. Seeing that his daughter-in-law had run home to report him, the old villager hurriedly called his wife back, confessed the whole truth, and asked how they could deal with it. The old woman thought to herself: "The girl's father is a simple rustic and won't come; only her mother, that fierce shrew, is sure to arrive." Having already hit upon a scheme to trap her, she turned and congratulated her old man instead: "Congratulations! A stroke of good luck has arrived!" The old villager said, "What's done was a mistake—don't mock me. You've always been resourceful, and I listen to you in everything. Save me now, or our family will be ruined!" The old woman said, "Ruined? It'll cost you your life! Yet if I save you now, you'll only grow bolder. If you obey me and swear never to harbor such wild thoughts again, I'll not only save you, I'll treat you to a fine piece of luck besides." The old villager said, "I don't ask for any luck—just save me this once, and I'll never dare think a wicked thought again. If I do, may Heaven strike me and Earth destroy me!" The old woman said, "Since you've sworn, I'll spare you this time. Take four taels of silver in two ingots, and hide in the outer guest room underneath the big vat. When the girl's mother arrives, I'll have her bathe in that room. Once she finishes washing, crawl out from under the vat and press the two silver ingots into her hands. She'll surely clutch the silver and won't be able to push you away; then force yourself on her once, walk right out, and the whole matter will be settled." The old villager said, "If I violate her too, won't that prove I really did harass her daughter?" The old woman said, "Never you mind—leave the rest to me." The old villager did as told and hid beneath the vat.

paragraphs.zh: 少顷，姻母到。老妈出外笑迎曰：“有劳贵步，未曾备轿迎得。”姻母便骂曰：“你家没伦理爬灰老贼，奸我女儿！”老妈故惊曰：“恰才哄我说，媳妇私煮炒吃，被他打骂，因逃归，乃有此恶事？我要和这老狗死！”大声大口，骂恨更切，姻母无待开口矣。因曰：“停会我、你、儿、媳四人，揪住打死，以大粪灌其口，使不为人。”即令媳妇把大鸡鸭宰，设盛馔待姻母。先大骂一场，后待茶果讫，曰：“走路身热，可讨水与洗澡，再好食午。”送姻母入房中洗，老妈入后厨房助妇整酒。及洗讫，下一人出，以银两锭付姻母，两手抱住便奸。及喊叫女儿、亲母，并无人应。其人曰：“她在厨房远，怎叫得知？”赤身难拒，又爱惜两槽银，哑口受奸。事讫，村老曰：“我就是亲家，你勿信女儿说。这成奸也是前缘，我本躲避你，谁知你送来洗澡，反先与你相好，从今再不望你女儿矣。”言罢走出。
paragraphs.en: Before long, the girl's mother arrived. The old woman came out with a welcoming smile and said, "Sorry to trouble your honored steps; we failed to prepare a sedan chair to meet you." The girl's mother immediately began cursing: "Your household has no decency! That old scoundrel of a father-in-law violated my daughter!" Feigning shock, the old woman cried, "Just now he fooled me by saying our daughter-in-law had secretly cooked herself a dish, and that she ran home because he beat and scolded her—how could he have done such a wicked thing? I'll have it out with that old dog to the death!" She cursed and railed at the top of her lungs, even more fiercely than her guest, leaving the girl's mother no room to get a word in. Then she said, "In a little while, you, I, my son, and my daughter-in-law—the four of us together—will seize him, beat him half to death, and pour nightsoil down his throat until he's unfit to show his face among men!" She ordered her daughter-in-law to slaughter plump chickens and ducks and lay out a lavish feast for her mother. After a round of loud cursing, they served tea and fruit, and the old woman said, "Walking in this heat makes one sticky; let us fetch water for you to bathe first, and then we can enjoy the midday meal in comfort." She ushered the girl's mother into the room to wash, while she herself went to the back kitchen to help her daughter-in-law warm the wine. Once the mother finished bathing, a man crawled out from beneath the vat, pressed two ingots of silver into her hands, threw his arms around her, and forced himself upon her. She cried out for her daughter and the old woman, but no one answered. The old villager said, "They are far off in the kitchen—how could they hear you?" Stripped for her bath, unable to break free, and reluctant to part with the two ingots of silver in her hands, she silently submitted to him. When it was over, the old villager said, "In-law, do not believe your daughter's tale. Our coming together today was also fated from a former life. I was hiding in here out of fear of you—who would have thought they would send you into this room to bathe, and that you and I would share this intimacy first? From now on, I will never harbor another thought toward your daughter." With that, he walked out.

paragraphs.zh: 姻母入厨，见女与老妈方在排馔，想叫时必是不闻，遂午间从容笑饮，不说及爬灰事矣。
paragraphs.en: The mother-in-law went into the kitchen, saw her daughter-in-law and the old maid still arranging the dishes, thinking they must not have heard her shouting, so at noon she drank and smiled at her ease, letting the matter of "climbing the ash" go unmentioned.

paragraphs.zh: 席罢辞归，老妈再三苦留，女亦曰：“我叫你来做身主，你只要人酒吃，何这等老懵？”姻母曰：“我妇人自身不能作主，怎能做得你主？你公公不是好人，你妈妈贤德。只姑媳不相离，自无恶事矣。”老妈留之不得，以食品果仪厚赠之，欢喜送别而去。凄风骤雨之景色，倏化为光风化日之风景，皆能妇调停之力，———亦一大棍也。
paragraphs.en: After the meal, she took her leave. The old lady repeatedly urged her to stay; the daughter also said, "I called you to be my host/sponsor; you only want to drink wine—how can you be such an old fool?" The mother-in-law replied, "As a woman, I cannot even make decisions for myself; how can I make them for you? Your father-in-law is no good, but your mother-in-law is virtuous. As long as the mother-in-law and daughter-in-law do not part ways, no evil will occur." Unable to keep her, the old lady gave generous gifts of food and fruit and happily saw her off. The scene of bitter wind and sudden rain suddenly transformed into bright breezes and fair sunshine—all thanks to this capable woman's mediation. She too was a great swindler.

paragraphs.zh: 按：妇人不可轻易往外亲之家。若彼狡妇与昵夫套合，中多有被其污秽者，谁则知之？若此村老妇之弄姻母，虽一时解纷之巧计，亦彼自知妇人性皆流水，可以利暗诱奸暗陷，必不敢张胆明言也。后人其鉴之。
paragraphs.en: Note: Women should not lightly visit their relatives by marriage. If a cunning woman colludes with her lover to set a trap, many are defiled—who would know? As with this old village woman tricking her mother-in-law: though it was a clever one-time ruse to settle a quarrel, she also knew that women’s hearts are as fickle as flowing water; they can be secretly lured by profit into a hidden snare for illicit affairs, yet dare not speak of it openly. Let future generations take warning.

stories.title_en: Climbing the Ashes: Cheating on the Mother-in-Law, Then Swindling Her

paragraphs.zh: 乡间有一佃户，欠主人苗三冬，算该本息银五两零。冬间，主人来收租，佃母与子谋曰：“苗带今年共欠三冬，明年必起田去，一家无望矣。我看主人富家子弟，必好风月，不如把媳妇哄他奸，拿住必可赖得苗去。”佃曰：“这事可。母亲可与媳妇言。”佃母曰：“还有一件，须要与他奸完了，然后拿住，他方甘心；若未成奸便拿，他是主人，怎肯受屈？又难赚他银矣。”佃曰：“亦可。”佃母方与媳妇言。妇曰：“你子心下实何如？”佃母曰：“我与儿说过了。任你事完成，然后拿他，方抵得苗去。”三人商议已定。
paragraphs.en: In the countryside there was a tenant who owed the landlord three winters of grain rent, calculated at over five taels principal and interest. In winter the landlord came to collect. The tenant’s mother plotted with her son: "With this year’s, we owe three winters of grain; next year he’ll surely take the land back, and the whole family will have no hope. I see the landlord is a rich family’s son—he must be fond of romance. Better have the daughter-in-law trick him into a tryst, catch him in the act, and we can cheat the debt away." The tenant said, "That can work. Mother, speak to the daughter-in-law." The mother said, "One more thing: he must finish the deed before we catch him, so he’ll submit. If we catch him before it’s done, he’s the landlord—why would he accept being wronged? And it’ll be hard to make off with his silver." The tenant said, "That’s fine too." The mother then spoke to the daughter-in-law. The wife asked, "What does your son truly think?" The mother said, "I’ve spoken with my son. Let you complete the act, then catch him, so it can offset the rent." The three agreed.

paragraphs.zh: 次日饭后，佃推往岳丈家借银来还苗。佃母又吩咐媳妇曰：“主人来无菜，我往上村讨斤肉，再往叔家取个鸡来。苗有还否，须做一东道与主人吃。你须备火炉与主人向。”主人在外已闻。二人去后，妇拾火炉出煽火。主人问曰：“你妈妈哪里去？”妇曰：“去讨菜。”又问曰：“你丈夫何去？”妇曰：“到我娘家去借银还你苗，未知有否？”主人曰：“不消问你娘借，只消问你借。”妇曰：“我若有银，早送来还了。”主曰：“昨夜早同我睡，便与你对苗去。”妇曰：“睡可当得银，今夜来陪你。”主人便起曰：“不待夜间，今日喜得无人，就耍去。你夫借得银来，我背地秤三钱与你买布；若无银，且宽限你明年还。”妇人即允，同入房去。佃户从密处窥见，悄悄出候房门外。只听房内二人欢话，心中自然焦燥，恨不得即打进去。半晌久，主人曰：“起去罢。”妇曰：“从容无妨。”知其完了，在房外高声喝曰：“你和甚人讲话？”打入门去。二人忙不能躲。佃户喝曰：“嗳也！你这贼奸我妻！”便在床上揪下打。妻忙起穿衣，来拿夫手曰：“你嫁我，我不在你家！”佃户曰：“这花娘也要打死！”三人滚作一团，也不能打得。佃母适携肉、鸡从外归，问曰：“何为？”佃曰：“主人奸我妻，我在床上拿住，我要打死这两个。”母指主人曰：“你好人家子孙也，不该干此事。不如讨银与我媳赔丑罢。”主人曰：“便对三年苗与你。”佃取妇脚带，系住主颈曰：“我不肯。”出外取刀磨曰：“定杀死他！”母出外抢刀，曰：“他是官家舍，白的是银，黄的是金，要得他几多。若杀死他，我你也不得安生。”再入劝主曰：“我儿性子不好，你再写田契与他。”主人曰：“亦可。”佃母取纸与写契。佃户立旁，勒要更写毗连田，共凑二十铺，作价二十两。主人亦写与之。佃母再与子商曰：“本意只抵赖苗，不意多得二十两。今晚你须避开，再令媳妇陪他一宵，方服得他心，可保无事。”佃曰：“已得娶妻之本，就让他一宵。”
paragraphs.en: Next day after the meal, the tenant pretended to go to his father-in-law’s house to borrow silver to repay the seed grain (miao) to the landlord. The mother also told her daughter-in-law: “When the master comes, there will be no dish; I’ll go to the upper village to beg for a jin of meat, then to my brother’s house to fetch a chicken. Whether the miao is repaid or not, we must host a meal for the master. You prepare a brazier for him to warm himself.” The master, standing outside, had already heard everything. After the two left, the wife brought out the brazier and fanned the fire. The master asked, “Where did your mother go?” The wife said, “To get dishes.” He asked again, “Where is your husband?” The wife said, “He went to my father-in-law’s to borrow silver to repay your miao; I don’t know if he’ll succeed.” The master said, “No need to borrow from your father-in-law; just borrow from you.” The wife said, “If I had silver, I would have sent it long ago.” The master said, “If you had slept with me last night, I would have settled the miao debt for you.” The wife said, “If sleeping can count as silver, come tonight and I’ll keep you company.” The master stood up: “Don’t wait for night; luckily there’s no one today—let’s play now. If your husband borrows the silver, I’ll secretly weigh out three qian for you to buy cloth; if there’s no silver, I’ll extend the deadline until next year.” The woman agreed; they went into the room. The tenant, watching from a hidden spot, quietly came out and waited outside the door. Hearing the two chatting happily inside, he was naturally agitated, wishing he could burst in immediately. After a long while, the master said, “Get up.” The wife said, “No hurry.” Knowing it was over, he shouted outside, “Who are you talking with?” and burst in. The two were too hurried to hide. The tenant shouted, “Ai! You thief—you’ve seduced my wife!” and dragged him off the bed to beat him. The wife hurriedly dressed, grabbed her husband’s hands: “You married me off; I’m not staying in your house!” The tenant said, “This hussy should be beaten to death too!” The three rolled in a heap; he couldn’t really beat them. Just then, the mother returned with meat and chicken: “What’s happening?” The tenant said, “The master seduced my wife; I caught them on the bed; I’ll beat these two to death.” The mother pointed at the master: “You’re a son of a good family; you shouldn’t do this. Better pay silver to my daughter-in-law to make up for the shame.” The master said, “I’ll write off three years’ worth of miao.” The tenant took the wife’s foot-binding, tied it around the master’s neck: “I won’t agree.” He went out, took a knife, and sharpened it: “I’ll kill him for sure!” The mother rushed out, snatched the knife: “He’s from an official family; silver and gold are plentiful—he has plenty to give. If you kill him, neither you nor I will live in peace.” She went back in and urged the master: “My son’s temper is bad; write him a land deed too.” The master said, “All right.” The mother fetched paper for him to write the deed. The tenant stood by and forced him to also write the adjoining fields, totaling twenty pu, priced at twenty taels. The master wrote that too. The mother conferred with her son again: “We only meant to write off the miao; unexpectedly we got twenty taels extra. Tonight you should stay away; let the daughter-in-law keep him company one night, so his heart submits and we can keep things safe.” The tenant said, “I’ve already recovered the cost of buying a wife; I’ll yield him one night.”

paragraphs.zh: 半午后，方整酒出。佃欲请人陪，佃母曰：“不可，只我老人自陪。”三人同坐，主人只索饭吃回去。佃母曰：“适间儿子蠢性，千万勿怪，我自陪你。”叫儿子先吃饭，往母舅家，故说借银，相添买田。儿去讫，佃母呼妇出陪。主人曰：“你母子妆套弄我，明日必告官理论。”佃母发誓曰：“我若套弄你，我即死在今日！”佃妇泣曰：“若告我便缢死。”主人见妇泣，翻料其非套，曰：“我不管你有套否，今晚更与我睡一夜，便当送你。”佃母连声应曰：“凭媳妇。”妇曰：“拼定陪你。男人若有言，嫁我便是。”主人被此瞒过，只宿一宵而去，安然无后话。
paragraphs.en: Late in the afternoon, they finally set out the wine. The tenant wished to invite others to join, but his mother said, "No; only I, an old woman, will keep him company." The three sat together, but the landlord merely asked for a meal and intended to return home. The mother then said, "My son was foolish just now; please do not take offense. I shall keep you company myself." She told her son to eat first and go to his maternal uncle’s house, pretending to borrow silver to help buy land. Once the son had left, the mother called the daughter-in-law out to keep the landlord company. The landlord said, "You mother and son have set a trap for me; tomorrow I will report this to the magistrate." The mother swore, "If I have tricked you, may I die this very day!" The daughter-in-law wept and said, "If you sue us, I will hang myself." Seeing her tears, the landlord reconsidered and thought it was no trap. He said, "I do not care whether there was a trap or not; sleep with me tonight, and I will let you go." The mother quickly agreed, "It is up to the daughter-in-law." The wife said, "I am determined to keep you company. If my husband speaks a word against it, then marry me." Fooled by this, the landlord stayed only one night and left; no further trouble arose.

paragraphs.zh: 按：佃母极狡猾，安排圈子已定，又令奸须过手，又令再陪一夜，方得主人心凉。不然，主佃之分，岂空套可笼？此佃母一狡棍也，述与后人知防。
paragraphs.en: Note: The tenant’s mother was extremely cunning. She had already set her trap, then made sure the illicit goods passed through her hands, and even demanded another night of company before the landlord finally felt satisfied. Otherwise, given the clear distinction between landlord and tenant, could mere empty words ever bind him? This tenant’s mother was a real master swindler; I recount this so future generations may know how to guard against such tricks.

stories.title_en: A Tenant’s Wife Sells Sex to Cheat the Landlord Out of His Land

paragraphs.zh: 荆南道上，人多畜马，以租行客，日收其利。有三妇轻身同行，遇马夫牵回马三匹，三妇各租乘一匹。末婶曰：“伯母善乘马者先行，我二人不善乘者随后。”行不十里，末婶叫马夫扶下马小宜。马夫紧抱以下，有讨趣之意。末婶曰：“你讨我便宜。”马夫曰：“不敢！要紧挟些，方不跌。”末婶曰：“看你亦知趣。我久无丈夫的，亦不怕你挟。”马夫曰：“既不怕，前有小茅房，再同我相抱一抱何如？”妇曰：“要赶路。今晚在你家借歇，何如？”马夫曰：“无三铺床。”妇曰：“伯母两人同榻，我只傍床。”马夫曰：“你要傍我床，我不索你租马银。”妇人曰：“人比马价，你又讨便宜。”马夫曰：“两有便宜事，可不好干。”
paragraphs.en: On the Jingnan roads, people often kept horses to rent out to travelers, collecting daily profit. Three women traveling light met a horse-handler leading back three horses; each woman rented one. The youngest said, "Auntie who rides well, go first; we two who don't ride well will follow." Before ten li, the youngest called the handler to help her down, pretending to need to ease herself. He held her tightly as he lowered her, with a hint of taking liberties. She said, "You're trying to take advantage." He replied, "I wouldn't dare! I must hold tight so you don't fall." She said, "I see you know your business. I've had no husband for long; I'm not afraid of your holding." He said, "If you're not afraid, there's a small thatched hut ahead; how about another hug?" She said, "We have to hurry. Tonight we'll lodge at your house—how about that?" He said, "I don't have three beds." She said, "The two aunts can share a couch; I'll just stay by your bed." He said, "If you'll stay by my bed, I won't charge you horse rent." She said, "Comparing a person to a horse's price—you're trying to take advantage again." He said, "When both sides get a bargain, why wouldn't we do it?"

paragraphs.zh: 两人正在此私约，前面次伯母坠马。妇指马夫曰：“快去扶我小姆。”马夫行且回顾曰：“不要哄我。”妇曰：“小姆若跌坏，怕她不在半路歇？我你事一定成矣。”马夫忙奔前去。
paragraphs.en: While they were making their secret arrangement, the woman's second-eldest uncle's wife ahead fell from her horse. The woman pointed at the groom: "Quick, go help my younger aunt." The groom walked forward but kept turning back: 'Don't try to trick me.' The woman said, "If the younger aunt gets badly hurt, she'll surely have to stop and rest on the road. Then our scheme is certain to succeed." The groom hurried off immediately.

paragraphs.zh: 次母跌在路盘坐，挪脚曰：“跌伤了脚，又跌伤了腿。”马夫扶起上马，曰：“须赶路。”次姆曰：“我跌坏了，前去须买补损膏药贴，只好随路歇，赶不得梢头。你前去叫我大姆少待。”因挨延北两遭，前马去不止十餘里。马夫向前去追，后二妇跃马加鞭奔回。
paragraphs.en: The middle one fell and sat cross-legged on the road, saying: "I've hurt my foot and my leg too." The handler helped her mount, saying: "We must hurry." The middle one replied: "I'm injured; ahead we'll have to buy bruise plaster. We can only rest along the way—we can't make the destination. You go ahead and tell my eldest aunt to wait a little." By stalling twice like this, the front horse was already more than ten li ahead. The handler went forward to catch up, while the two women behind whipped their horses and raced back.

paragraphs.zh: 马夫前去赶不上，心忖曰：“任她前去，且在此等后二妇来，她自然要等齐同歇矣。”俟久不至，心又忖曰：“想必后路买膏药来。”因问行路人曰：“两妇人骑马的，到哪里了？”路人曰：“两妇人跑马如飞，此去不止二十里了。”马夫又问曰：“骑马是来此的，是去的？”路人曰：“是下去的。你快赶也来不及了。”马夫心无主意，慌忙走回原所，再问路人，皆云：“马去已远。”马夫追回十里，天已晚。再问行人，云：“不见妇人马矣。”三马从两路脱去，前后不能两追，马夫惟怅悒而归。
paragraphs.en: The handler couldn't catch the one ahead and thought: "Let her go on; I'll wait here for the two behind; they'll naturally wait to lodge together." He waited a long time; they didn't come. He thought again: "They must be buying plaster on the back road." He asked a passerby: "The two women on horses—where have they gotten to?" The passerby said, "The two women are racing like the wind; they're more than twenty li that way." The handler asked again: "Were they riding this way or going away?" The passerby said, "Going back down. Even if you hurry you won't catch them." The handler had no plan, hurried back to the original place, asked more people; all said, "The horses are already far." He chased back ten li; it was already dark. He asked travelers again; they said they hadn't seen the women or horses. The three horses had made off on two roads; he couldn't chase both front and back. The handler could only head home dejected.

paragraphs.zh: 按：此巧脱处全在后妇小宜，与马夫私谈，以惑其心，以缠其时；次又中妇跌马，彼疑真不善骑者，又缠多时，则前马稳脱矣，故赚其前追，又安能及？后两妇奔回，彼唯疑跌伤来迟，岂料反奔而回乎？然亦马夫太痴：安有中途一遇，便许与你歇？马夫有何标致而妇恋之？其言太甘，其中必毒。故就其甜言处，便知是棍也。以妇人而有此高手，世道几何不鬼魅哉！
paragraphs.en: Note: The clever getaway hinged entirely on the rear woman using a minor pretext to talk privately with the groom, confusing his mind and wasting his time; then the middle woman fell from her horse, making him suspect she truly couldn't ride, wasting even more time, while the front horse got away steadily. Thus they lured him to chase ahead—how could he catch up? The two behind raced back; he only thought the injured one was slow, never guessing they were racing the other way! But the groom was too foolish: who, meeting halfway, would immediately promise to let you stay? What charm did the groom possess that women would cling to him? Words too sweet hide poison. From the sweet talk itself, you know it's a swindle. When women possess such mastery, how can the world not be full of demons?

stories.title_en: Three Women Make Off with Three Horses

paragraphs.zh: 白鉴妻向氏，大有姿色。鉴专好酒，与妻不甚绸缪。为王军门公干，差之上京。妻向氏在家开纸马店，常遣婢兰香接钱交易。夫去日久，向氏时出店看人。有宁朝贤见之，爱其美，注目看之；向亦不避。朝贤归，与心友曹知高谋，欲诱此妇。曹曰：“若骗妇人，须用一女人在内行事，方易成就。古云‘山贼攻山贼，水寇擒水寇’。此中法华庵尼姑妙真，常往来各家，汝去托之，其事易矣。”朝贤闻教大喜，即寻法华庵来，见了妙真，以银二两送之，托其通纸马店内白鉴之妻；若事成之后，再有重谢。尼姑曰：“此也不难，你三日后来讨回音。”宁再三嘱之而去。
paragraphs.en: Bai Jian's wife, née Xiang, was very attractive. Jian loved wine and paid little attention to his wife. On business for Commander Wang, he was sent to the capital. While at home, Wife Xiang ran a paper-offering shop and often sent her maid Lanxiang to collect money and handle sales. With her husband gone for a long time, Xiang sometimes came out of the shop to gaze at passersby. Ning Chaoxian saw her, admired her beauty, and stared; Xiang did not avoid him. Chaoxian returned home and plotted with his close friend Cao Zhigao to lure this woman. Cao said, "To trick a woman, you need a woman working inside to make it easy. As the old saying goes: a mountain thief fights a mountain thief, a water pirate catches a water pirate. Nun Miaozhen of Fahua Convent often visits various households; go ask her, and the matter will be easy." Chaoxian was delighted, went to Fahua Convent, met Miaozhen, gave her two taels, and asked her to make contact with Bai Jian's wife in the paper-offering shop; if successful, there would be further heavy thanks. The nun said, "Not hard; come back in three days for a reply." Ning urged her repeatedly before leaving.

paragraphs.zh: 尼姑将手中数珠剪断绳子，捻定在手，往白鉴店前转行几次，不见向氏，空回了。次日又往，见向氏在店坐。尼姑故将断绳珠撒放满地，多有滚在污泥去者，俯躬满地捡之。向氏见，叫之入，以水与洗，又净手讫。尼姑再三拜谢而去。
paragraphs.en: The nun cut the string of the prayer beads in her hand and twisted them tight. She paced back and forth several times in front of Bai Jian's shop but found no sign of Xiang, so she returned empty-handed. The next day she went again and saw Xiang sitting in the shop. Deliberately, the nun scattered the broken-string beads all over the ground; many rolled into the mud. She bent down to gather them from everywhere. Seeing this, Xiang called her inside, gave her water to wash, and the nun cleaned her hands thoroughly. The nun bowed repeatedly to thank her before departing.

paragraphs.zh: 至明日，尼姑买糕、果、饼、面四品，叫人往向氏家谢。向氏喜，遣人请尼姑来吃素酒。席间，向氏问曰：“你几岁出家？”尼姑曰：“我半路出家。”向曰：“因何事出家？”尼曰：“因嫁个人，好赌钱饮酒，终日在外，有夫与无夫同，故誓愿出家。”向氏叹气一声道：“招这人不如勿嫁。”尼见他动心，又问曰：“娘子如何叹气？”赂曰：“我病亦似你。今嫁个人，只好饮酒，从来不要妻子，一年不欢会几次。今又奉差远去，似无夫一般。”尼知此妇有春怨，即乘机曰：“男人心歹者多。唯我庵前宁朝贤，当日爱妻如命，只其妻没福而死。今央我择再娶，谁妇人遇此者，真日日得欢喜也。”向氏听了，口中不语。尼亦不好再调，酒完而去。
paragraphs.en: The next day, the nun bought four items—cakes, fruit, pastries, and noodles—and sent someone to Xiang's house to express gratitude. Xiang was pleased and invited the nun over for a vegetarian meal with wine. At the table, Xiang asked, "At what age did you leave home?" The nun replied, "Midway through my life." Xiang asked, "Why?" The nun said, "I married a man who loved gambling and drinking, always out all day; having a husband was no different from having none, so I vowed to enter the convent." Xiang sighed, "Better not to marry than to marry such a man." Seeing she had moved her, the nun asked, "Why does Madam sigh?" Xiang replied, "My plight is much like yours. I married a man who only cares for drinking and never wants his wife; we don't even meet happily a few times a year. Now he has been sent far away on an official mission; it's as if I have no husband at all." Knowing the woman harbored wifely loneliness, the nun seized the moment: "Many men are wicked at heart. But Ning Chaoxian, whose temple is right before mine, loved his wife as his own life. Alas, she lacked fortune and died. Now he asks me to find him a new wife; any woman who meets him would truly be happy every single day." Xiang heard this but said nothing. The nun dared not press further; after the meal, she departed.

paragraphs.zh: 第三日，朝贤整饰衣冠，来庵问回音，妙真曰：“事有九分成了。凡妇人与夫和顺者，极难挑动。昨向氏请我，知她心中恨夫；又别夫日久，但有机会，便可到手。今须讨银与我，办一盛席，请来用好酒灌醉，必在我床睡，你便解开衣，慢慢行事，恣你所为矣。但醒来之时，须备镯甸簪珥类送之，可买其心，方可长久相交。”宁听了拜下：“若如此，死生不忘。今再送银五两，你速作席请来。”
paragraphs.en: On the third day, Chaoxian dressed up and came to the convent for a reply. Miaozhen said, "Nine-tenths done. Women who get along with their husbands are very hard to stir. Yesterday Xiang invited me; I learned she resents her husband; and she’s been apart from him a long time; given a chance, she’s within grasp. Now I need silver; I’ll prepare a rich feast, invite her, pour good wine till she’s drunk; she’ll sleep in my bed; you unfasten her garments and slowly proceed, do as you please. But when she wakes, have bracelets, bangles, hairpins, and earrings ready to give her, to buy her heart, so you can maintain a long affair." Ning bowed: "If so, I won’t forget this in life or death. Here’s five more taels; quickly make the feast and invite her."

paragraphs.zh: 妙真遣人买好肴好酒，叫厨子整治丰洁，先遣人去请，后自到家邀行。向氏欢喜，同兰香打轿而来。见酒席十分美盛，曰：“你还请何人？”妙真曰：“专请娘子，并无别客。”向氏曰：“一人亦不消如此破费，怎吃得许多？”妙真曰：“我无亲骨肉，多感娘子知己，愿结为姊妹，当个知心人。”向氏笑曰：“我和你知心，不能相爬痒痛。”饮了几杯，问曰：“此酒香而甜，其价必贵。”尼曰：“是前日宁大官送的，亦不识其价。”又劝饮。向氏曰：“酒甜吃得下，只恐易醉。”尼曰：“若醉暂在我房少睡，醒后回去不迟。不知娘子尊量，饮几许方醉。”向氏曰：“夜间恐睡不着，常可饮一瓶。若不饮酒，如何得睡？”尼曰：“若自家人在家，只吃他一杯，便可睡矣。”向氏曰：“我和你说知心话，虽醉只半夜便醒。丈夫在家，只是贪酒，再不要干事。我醒来极是难熬，哪止得我渴想？”妙真曰：“似此有老公的，与我无有的一般。我日间犹过了，只夜来过不得，惟怨前生未修种也。”向曰：“的是如此。今日须极醉，求一夜可忘却。”少顷醉倒，遣兰香先回看家，旋在尼床少睡。
paragraphs.en: Miaozhen sent people to buy fine food and wine, had a cook prepare a rich and clean feast, first sending someone to invite, then going herself to fetch her. Xiang was delighted and came with Lanxiang in a sedan. Seeing the feast so lavish, she asked, "Who else did you invite?" Miaozhen replied, "Only Madam; no other guest." Xiang said, "For one person you needn't spend so much; how can we eat that much?" Miaozhen said, "I have no blood kin; I am grateful that Madam is a kindred spirit; I wish to become sisters, a true confidante." Xiang laughed, "You and I are confidantes, yet we cannot satisfy each other's needs." After a few cups, she asked, "This wine is fragrant and sweet; it must be expensive." The nun said, "Master Ning sent it the other day; I don't know its price." She urged her to drink more. Xiang said, "It's sweet and goes down easily, but I fear I'll get drunk quickly." The nun said, "If you get drunk, sleep a while in my room; head home after you wake, no rush. I don't know Madam's capacity—how much before you're drunk?" Xiang said, "At night if I can't sleep, I often drink a bottle. If I don't drink, how can I sleep?" The nun said, "If your husband were at home, just one cup from him would make you sleepy." Xiang said, "Let me tell you a truth between confidantes: even when drunk, I wake by midnight. My husband at home only greedily drinks and never wants to perform his duty. When I wake, it's unbearable—how can that quench my thirst?" Miaozhen said, "So having a husband is like having none. Daytime I can still endure; only nights I cannot; I only resent not planting merit in a past life." Xiang said, "Exactly so. Today I must get very drunk, hoping for one night of forgetting." Soon she collapsed drunk. Miaozhen sent Lanxiang home first to watch the house, then Xiang slept a while on the nun's bed.

paragraphs.zh: 朝贤向氏睡，即来解其衣带，如死去而暖的一样，凭他恣意恋战，其味甚美。少歇又一次，亦不醒。朝贤双手搂定妇人睡，直到半夜醒来，衣已脱去。觉有男子在身边，又觉腰间爽快，浑身通泰，低声问道：“你是何人？”朝贤道：“心肝，我想你几时，今日方才得偷两次，还要明日和我一好。”向氏曰：“你谋既就，切不可与外人知。”朝贤曰：“只尼姑知道，除外何人得知？”
paragraphs.en: While Lady Xiang was fast asleep, Chaoxian came in and undid her sash and clothes. She lay there like one dead, yet warm to the touch; he took his pleasure of her as he pleased, finding it utterly delightful. After a brief rest, he had his way a second time, and still she did not wake. Chaoxian held her tightly in both arms and slept until midnight. When she finally awoke, her clothes had already been taken off. Feeling a man lying beside her, a pleasant ease at her waist, and her whole body relaxed and refreshed, she whispered, "Who are you?" Chaoxian replied, "My darling, how long I have longed for you! Today I finally managed to steal two trysts with you—tomorrow you must be good to me again." Lady Xiang said, "Now that your scheme has succeeded, you must never let outsiders know." Chaoxian said, "Only the nun knows; who else could possibly find out?"

paragraphs.zh: 又睡到天微明，向氏起。朝贤以镯甸与之，又抱亲嘴。两人兴浓，再战一次，携手出门。妙真已在候，忍笑不住，曰：“好酒也！”向氏曰：“好计也！”朝贤曰：“好姻缘也！”妙真曰：“既有此好，何以谢我？”紧抱贤曰：“亏我脚酸也，要和我好为谢。”贤曰：“力尽耳，今夜不忘谢。”向氏曰：“从今夜夜都让谢你。”朝贤曰：“后会可长，谢亦可长。”从此常与向氏往来，皆由尼姑此番之引诱也。
paragraphs.en: They slept until faint dawn; Xiang rose. Chaoxian gave her bracelets and embraced her, kissing her deeply. Still full of passion, they engaged once more, then went out hand in hand. Miaozhen was already waiting, unable to hold back her laughter, saying, "Good wine!" Xiang replied, "Good scheme!" Chaoxian declared, "What a perfect union!" Miaozhen asked, "Since it's so good, how will you thank me?" She hugged Chaoxian tightly: "My legs ache from all this work; be good with me as my reward." Chaoxian said, "I'm spent; I won't forget to thank you tonight." Xiang added, "From tonight on, we'll owe you every single night." Chaoxian remarked, "Our meetings can last long; our thanks can too." From then on, he frequently visited Xiang, entirely due to this seduction by the nun.

paragraphs.zh: 按：妇人虽贞，倘遇淫妇引之，无不入于邪者。凡妇之谨身，唯知耻耳，唯畏人知耳。苟一失身之后，耻心既丧，又何所不为？故人家唯慎尼姑、媒婆等，勿使往来，亦防微杜渐之正道也。
paragraphs.en: Note: Even a chaste woman, if led by a wanton woman, will enter into evil. A woman’s guarding her person is only knowing shame, only fearing people will know. Once she’s lost herself, shame is gone—what won’t she do? So households should be careful with nuns, matchmakers, and the like; don’t let them come and go. This is the right way to stop trouble at the start.

stories.title_en: A Nun Scatters Prayer Beads to Lure a Woman into an Illicit Affair

paragraphs.zh: 浙中有等棍，常於通衢僻路，專候人家子女十數歲者，或迷路失歸，必拐帶去。擇其女有姿色，又絕聰明者，賣落院為娼。稍愚鈍者，刺瞎其雙眼，教之唱叫路歌曲；又或刖去足掌，致其拐腳。其刖足之法，每於隆冬極寒時，以麻扎幼童足肚，置腳掌於冷水中。浸得良久，以柴木指之曰：「痛否？」童應曰：「痛。」則又浸，及至冷極血凝，指亦不知痛，則以利刃刖斷其足掌，然後用藥敷之。後驅此雙瞽者、拐腳者，叫乞於道，每日責其丐錢米。多者與之飽食，少者痛酷捶打，令乞者方肯哀丐。晚复聚宿舟中。棍得其錢米，置美衣美食，在舟中歌唱為樂。暇或登岸，又四出拐帶，極為民害，而人不知。
paragraphs.en: In Zhejiang there is a gang of swindlers who haunt busy thoroughfares and lonely byways, waiting for children of ten years or so belonging to others. Any child who loses their way home is sure to be carried off. They pick out girls who are pretty and quick-witted and sell them into brothels as prostitutes. The duller ones they blind in both eyes and teach to sing begging songs along the road; or they sever their feet at the ankle to leave the child lame. Their method of amputation is this: in deepest winter, when the cold is most bitter, they bind a child’s calves with hemp and set the feet in cold water. After a long soak they prod them with a stick of firewood and ask, “Does it hurt?” If the child answers, “It hurts,” they soak them longer, until the cold has congealed the blood and the prodding no longer hurts; then they slice off the foot with a sharp blade and dress the wound with medicine. Afterward they drive these blind and crippled children onto the roads to beg, demanding a daily take of money and rice. Those who bring back plenty get a full meal; those who bring back little are savagely beaten, so the young beggars learn to plead piteously. At night they all gather to sleep in a boat. The swindlers pocket the money and rice, dress in fine clothes, eat well, and amuse themselves singing on board. In idle hours they go ashore and fan out to kidnap more children. They are a monstrous plague on the people, and no one knows it.

paragraphs.zh: 一日，有小丐婆唱叫於路。居旁一老婦曰：「此丐婆好似李意五之女，其聲音亦似，只目瞎耳。」丐婆曰：「吾父正是李意五，吾有哥名鴉兒。五年前我往外婆家，不識路，被人引去，刺瞎兩眼，每日遣出叫化。有錢米歸，則有食；丐得稀少，便痛打無食，極是苦楚無奈。你聲音似我鄰居王二姆一般，千萬叫我娘與哥來認我，超度我出此地獄，你陰功如天。」王二姆聽其敘來歷皆真，收留入家曰：「你母今年已死，你兄遷居上巷，即遣人去喚來。」彼此皆相認得，遂具狀告於縣，批與主簿審。差人船中提二棍到。棍即用銀賄主簿；又用銀二十兩買其兄李鴉兒曰：「你令妹是他人拐帶，我收與眾乞合夥，非我刺她眼。況今已雙瞽，亦無人娶，不如與丐子為伴，亦不虧她衣食。」兄與官都得銀了，拘審時哥不堅認，主簿仍斷與棍去。棍引到船，撐入湖心痛打，以儆他丐，使後不敢漏洩。李丐婆叫屈連天，淒楚不忍聞。
paragraphs.en: One day, a female beggar was singing for alms on the road. An old woman living nearby said, "This beggar looks just like Li Yiwu's daughter—and her voice is like hers too, only she is blind." The beggar replied, "My father is indeed Li Yiwu; I have a brother named Ya'er. Five years ago, while going to my grandmother's house, I didn't know the way and was led away by someone who stabbed out both my eyes. Since then, he sends me out begging daily. If I bring back money and rice, I get food; if I collect little, I am beaten and starved—my suffering is unbearable. Your voice sounds exactly like my neighbor Auntie Wang Er. Please call my mother and brother to identify me and rescue me from this hell; your hidden merit will be as vast as Heaven." Auntie Wang Er heard her story and found every detail true. She took her home and said, "Your mother died this year, and your brother has moved to Upper Lane; I will send for him at once." They recognized each other immediately and filed a complaint with the county magistrate, who assigned it to the registrar for trial. Officials brought the two swindlers from their boat. The swindlers immediately bribed the registrar with silver, and paid another twenty taels to buy off the brother, Li Ya'er, saying, "Your sister was kidnapped by someone else; I merely took her in to join my band of beggars—it was not I who blinded her. Besides, she is now blind in both eyes and no one will marry her. It is better she stay with the beggars as a companion; she will not lack food or clothing." Having taken the silver, both the brother and the registrar failed to uphold the truth during the hearing, and the registrar ruled to return the girl to the swindlers. They took her to the boat, rowed out into the middle of the lake, and beat her savagely as a warning to other beggars never to let the secret out. Beggar Li cried her innocence to high heaven; the anguish was unbearable to hear.

paragraphs.zh: 船到向鄉官後門，聞溪中叫死聲，甚可憐，遣二家人去牽其船來，問打何人。眾丐指曰：「打李丐婆。」鄉官問：「因何打？」丐婆不敢說，只苦情求救。鄉官令引丐婆異處，再問曰：「你因何被這等苦打？明說來，我便救你。」李丐婆一一敘其前由。向鄉官聞情淒愴，不勝發忿，即鎖住四棍，並引眾丐入見太府，代陳其冤苦。太府亦切恨之，將四棍各打三十，曰：「此罪雖凌遲碎剮未足懲其罪，可鎖於府前，令眾人共毆之，以洩其忿。」眾人知此棍情，都來手毆石打，四棍一時皮破血吐，立刻盡死。後瞽目、拐腳眾丐，各問其鄉貫，家有人者，令其收養；無親屬者，各送入養濟院。人盡感向鄉官之仁，能除此四孽棍。
paragraphs.en: The boat happened to come by the back gate of a retired official named Xiang. Hearing cries of mortal agony from the creek—pitiful beyond words—he sent two servants to haul the boat in and asked who was being beaten. The beggars pointed and said, “They are beating the beggar woman Li.” The official asked why. The woman dared not say; she only begged in her misery to be saved. He had her led apart from the others and asked again: “Why were you beaten so cruelly? Tell me plainly, and I will save you.” The beggar woman Li told the whole story from the beginning. Hearing it, Xiang was grief-stricken and could not contain his fury. He clapped the four crooks in chains on the spot, led the whole band of beggars in to see the prefect, and laid out their wrongs on their behalf. The prefect too burned with hatred. He had each of the four given thirty strokes and declared: “For a crime like this, even death by slow slicing would not be punishment enough. Chain them in front of the prefecture gate and let the crowd beat them, to vent the people’s rage.” Everyone who knew what these crooks had done came to strike them with fists and stones; in moments the four were torn and vomiting blood, and all died on the spot. Afterward, the blind and crippled beggars were each asked their native place. Those with families were sent home to be cared for; those without kin were placed in poorhouses. The people were all grateful for Xiang’s humanity in rooting out these four swindling fiends.

paragraphs.zh: 按：人家子女幼稚，不可令其單行，亦不可帶金銀鐲錢。若偶遇此等棍，悔何可及！其防於未失之先可也。今後官府遇瞎拐群集處時，遣人查其居止，及提問一二瘸瞎緣由，或訪得此等棍，則除一棍勝去一狼虎也，功德高於浮屠矣。
paragraphs.en: Note: People with young children must never let them go about alone, nor let them wear gold or silver bangles. Should a child chance to meet such crooks, regret comes too late. Guard against the loss before it happens. Henceforth, whenever officials come upon a place where blind and crippled beggars gather, they should send men to find out where they lodge and question one or two of them about how they came to be lame or blind. If crooks like these are unearthed, then removing one crook is better than removing a wolf or a tiger—and the merit of it is higher than any pagoda.

stories.title_en: Blinding and Maiming: The Swindle of Crippling Victims

paragraphs.zh: 朝廷往往聽言利之臣，命太監四出抽分，名為徵商抑末以重農本，實則商稅重而轉賣之處必貴，則買之價增，而買者受其害；商不通而出物之處必賤，則賣之價減，而賣者受其害。利雖僅取及商，而四民皆陰耗其財，以供朝廷之暗取，尤甚於明加田稅也。且徵榷之利，朝廷得一，太監得十，稅官得百，巡卒得千，是民費千百金，以奉朝廷之一金，益上者少而損下者無涯矣。然巡卒、稅官之實溪壑，猶是普天率土之民得飽暖也。特不耕不織而魚肉下民，不免坐蠹天地間服食。若太監攘剝既多，崇聚盈溢，視錦繡如敝葉，視金玉如瓦礫。服食器用，皆與天子同；指使承順，如奉天子同。人間福分享受，無不窮極；獨恨不能淫樂女色，所少者此耳。嘗命左右，訪有復生陽物之方，購以萬金。
paragraphs.en: The court time and again heeds ministers who preach profit and sends eunuchs out across the country to levy duties on goods—in the name of “taxing merchants and curbing the secondary trades to strengthen agriculture, the root.” In truth, when taxes on trade are heavy, goods grow dear wherever they are resold: prices rise for the buyer, and the buyer suffers. When trade stops moving, goods grow cheap where they are produced: prices fall for the seller, and the seller suffers. The profit may seem to come only from merchants, but all four classes of the people are silently bled of their wealth to feed the court’s hidden exactions—worse than openly raising the land tax. Worse still, of every levy taken, the court gets one share, the eunuch ten, the tax officials a hundred, and the patrol guards a thousand. So the people pay out hundreds or thousands of taels to deliver a single tael to the court: little gained above, measureless harm below. And yet, when runners and tax clerks stuff their bottomless gullets, at least it is folk of this same realm who get fed and warmed. But men who neither plow nor weave and yet make fish and meat of the common people are nothing but grubs, battening on the food and clothing of the world. As for the eunuchs: having plundered and squeezed until their hoards pile high and overflow, they look on brocade as dead leaves and on gold and jade as rubble. Their dress, their food, their vessels all match the Son of Heaven’s, and the minions at their beck and call wait on them as they would wait on the Son of Heaven. Of every blessing and pleasure the human world holds, they enjoy the uttermost; their one regret is that they cannot have the pleasure of women—that alone is denied them. One of them once bade his attendants hunt for a method to regrow the male organ, with ten thousand taels as the reward.
